papers.title: Altered Inhibitory Control Across Subclinical Depression and Major Depressive Disorder: Evidence From Stroop Tasks and Diffusion Modeling
papers.reason: The paper uses Stroop tasks with drift diffusion and conflict diffusion modelling to estimate latent inhibitory-control parameters across depression severity groups.

papers.title: Non-invasive skin trace elementomics reveals a characteristic pattern of essential element deficiency and toxic element accumulation in children with ADHD.
papers.reason: The paper concerns a biological marker for ADHD status but does not appear to model or measure executive function, attention tasks, EEG, eye tracking, or behavioural cognition directly.

papers.title: How Task Load Modulates the Effect of State Anxiety on Working Memory and Its Neural Mechanisms: Evidence from Verbal and Spatial Modalities.
papers.reason: The title indicates an empirical study of working memory load, anxiety, and neural mechanisms across verbal and spatial modalities, directly relevant to executive-function neuroscience.

papers.title: Neural evidence for progressive decline of visual face recognition ability in Alzheimer’s disease
papers.reason: The study uses task-based FPVS-EEG to distinguish cognitive processing changes across cognitively unimpaired, MCI due to AD, and AD dementia groups, although the target process is face recognition rather than executive function.

papers.title: Longitudinal Non-Pharmacological Neuromodulation and Cognitive Training Across Sequential Intervention Studies in a Participant with Alzheimer’s Disease: A 10-Year Single-Participant Analysis
papers.reason: The paper tracks cognitive outcomes during long-term neuromodulation and cognitive training in AD, but it is an uncontrolled single-participant intervention report rather than an executive-function model or diagnostic biomarker method.

papers.title: Learning to Pursue Goals that Conflict with Prior Experience Relies on Fast Revaluation and Slow Value Updating
papers.reason: The paper develops and fits a computational model of human goal-directed learning with fast goal switching and slow value updating, directly targeting flexible cognitive control and decision making.

papers.title: Reconfiguration of the Cognitive Control Network Induced by Cerebral and Cerebro–Cerebellar Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation
papers.reason: The paper reports human fMRI, effective-connectivity, graph, and drift-diffusion findings on cognitive control networks and switching costs, providing directly model-relevant neuroscience evidence.
